canonicalReview.reconciliationSummary: Both independent reviewers returned pass with zero blocking findings, so there were no blockers to adjudicate. The reverifier independently re-verified every evidence citation behind reviewer-1's four non-blocking findings against the current code and artifacts: the fill-walk stop and chunk-candidacy predicate (select.ts:430-451, 471-485) plus coveredFrom as min over included entries' startOrder (select.ts:506-509) confirm E03-R1-001 mechanically, and the ruling artifact (artifacts/02-smart-compact/story-lead/001-ruling-response-001.json) exists and names the rejected 'smooth-obligate'/'partial-chunk' interpretations; cli/view.ts:20 and cli/index.ts:270 call domain surfaces directly while tech-design.md Flow 4 and the module matrix say the CLI builds an SDK, confirming E03-R1-002 as doc-vs-mechanism drift; thread-view/index.ts:403 stamps created_at with new Date().toISOString() while boundary.ts uses the injected clock, confirming E03-R1-003; openThreadDatabase runs migrations on every open (threads/internal/create.ts:191-205), confirming E03-R1-004. Architecture spot checks also confirmed reviewer-1's pass-supporting claims: the advance registers throw-isolated on ctx.onCommit ahead of the queue pokes (intake-stream/internal/pipeline.ts:150-158) and never-backward is enforced both in the decision and in the UPDATE's WHERE position < ? clause (boundary.ts:145-152). The epic gate was re-run fresh by the reverifier: pnpm run verify-all exited 0 with 38 test files and 325 tests passing. Reviewer-2's coarser-grained pass contains no claim that conflicts with reviewer-1; its absence of non-blocking findings is a granularity difference, not a dispute, so reviewer-1's four evidence-supported non-blocking findings are retained as the canonical set. No new regressions surfaced and no scope was widened beyond the prior canonical findings.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Literal selection rules can leave straddling turns unrepresented between smooth and detailed bands
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: Independently re-verified: chunk candidacy requires the chunk's newest live member to be strictly older than the oldest included smooth turn (select.ts:471-485, newestMember.turnOrder < oldestSmoothOrder) while the smooth fill stops at the first budget-crossing entry (fillBand, select.ts:430-451). Turns in the smooth remainder belonging to a straddling chunk — or closed-unchunked turns falling off the smooth share — get no band entry and no gap record, while coveredFrom is computed as the min over included entries' startOrder (select.ts:506-509) and can span them, so the omission is invisible in the receipt. The ruling artifact (artifacts/02-smart-compact/story-lead/001-ruling-response-001.json) exists and explicitly rejects the compensating 'smooth-obligate'/'partial-chunk' interpretations, requiring the literal rules — human-sanctioned behavior, transient (the next compact after chunking catches up re-covers the span), record-preserving (AC-2.9), but in tension with the epic's 'never silently omits a span' language; on record for the next design round.

nonBlockingFindings.title: CLI wires view commands and intake to domain surfaces directly rather than building an SDK as the tech design sketch states
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: Independently re-verified: tech design Flow 4 says 'The CLI builds a real SDK (cli/work.ts pattern)' and the module matrix lists cli/view.ts depending on 'sdk', but cli/view.ts imports the thread-view domain directly (src/cli/view.ts:20, with a header comment documenting the choice) and CLI intake calls intakeStream.messageEvents directly (src/cli/index.ts:270), relying on the design's own sanctioned below-SDK default-config fallback (thread-view/index.ts:71-75). Behavior is identical — no CLI view-config channel exists this epic, the operations are provider-free, and the process-suite leg proves CLI intake advances the boundary — so this is documentation-vs-mechanism drift, resolvable by a one-line tech-design correction or by wiring the CLI through createSdk later.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Compact stamps created_at from the real clock rather than the SDK's injected clock
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: Independently re-verified: src/domains/thread-view/index.ts:403 uses new Date().toISOString() for the view's created_at while the boundary advance uses the injected clock (boundary.ts:152, clock().toISOString()). Determinism is unaffected — view_id derives from maxEventOrder and materialize's generated fields derive from the stored created_at — and the team dispositioned the same shape as accepted-risk for the Story 0 migration seed timestamp. Threading the instance clock through compact would close the small consistency gap.

nonBlockingFindings.title: First pull/status on a pre-v6 thread file performs the one-time schema migration write
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: Independently re-verified: openThreadDatabase brings a thread file to the current schema version on every open (src/domains/threads/internal/create.ts:191-205, runMigrations after validateThreadFile), so a pull or status against a file recorded under Epic 02's v5 performs the v6 migration before reading — a write on what AC-1.1 calls a no-writes path. This is the inherited Epic 01/02 migration-on-open convention, necessary for the view_boundary singleton to exist, idempotent, and one-time; recorded so the convention's interaction with the reads-only contract is an explicit acceptance rather than an unnoticed one.
